title: Clinical Mastery: Ocular Toxocariasis (OT)
summary: Ocular toxocariasis is a parasitic infection caused by the larval stage of the roundworm Toxocara canis or cati, typically resulting in unilateral granulomatous inflammation. This guide covers the spectrum from subclinical peripheral granulomas to severe endophthalmitis.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Ocular toxocariasis is the ocular manifestation of visceral larva migrans. It is caused by accidental ingestion of embryonated T. canis (most common) or T. cati eggs. Incidence is highest in children aged 5-10 years. Prevalence studies suggest up to 10-20% of the healthy population may be seropositive, though clinical disease is rare.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect
content: Unilateral leukocoria in a child
Unexplained unilateral uveitis
History of pica or contact with puppies
Peripheral retinal traction bands leading to drag of the macula
Evidence of subretinal abscess

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Detailed history (puppy exposure/pica).
Step 2: Slit-lamp exam (check for anterior chamber cells).
Step 3: Indirect ophthalmoscopy (peripheral granuloma).
Step 4: Serology (ELISA for anti-Toxocara IgG).
Step 5: B-scan USG (r/o vitritis/traction).

content.explanation: P: Peripheral Granuloma, U: Unilateral, P: Pica history, P: Parasitic etiology, Y: Young age (children).

sections.title: Treatment Protocol
content: Systemic corticosteroids (mainstay to control inflammation).
Anti-helminthics (Albendazole 400mg BID for 5-14 days) - Controversial, may cause inflammation if larva dies in situ.
Pars plana vitrectomy for severe vitreous traction/epiretinal membrane.
Laser photocoagulation for localized peripheral granulomas.

sections.title: Complications
content: Tractional retinal detachment (TRD) due to fibrous bands.
Permanent vision loss due to macular heterotopia/drag.
Chronic glaucoma from anterior segment inflammation.
Cataract formation from chronic uveitis.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Peripheral granulomas are often misdiagnosed as 'pars planitis'.
Serology may be negative in Ocular Toxocariasis because the parasite burden is low; serum IgG titers are less sensitive than in Visceral Larva Migrans.
Always perform a baseline B-scan in patients with unilateral vitritis of unknown origin in children.
Avoid aggressive anti-parasitic treatment without concomitant corticosteroids.
